issues.body:
Line 2455 resolves the actionlint pin from $tree_scripts/actionlint.pin, so the diff under review selects the linter that judges it. The integrity constraints do hold: _actionlint_pin's ACTIONLINT_VERSION shape is '[0-9]+(\.[0-9]+)*' (no slashes, no '..'), the host and release path are fixed literals, and both the tarball and the extracted-binary sha256 are verified, so a candidate cannot execute arbitrary bytes.

What it CAN do is name a genuine but ANCIENT actionlint release with matching digests and lint its own workflow change with a linter that lacks the rule that would have caught it.

Not introduced here: I confirmed pr-gate.yml:176 sets `pin=scripts/actionlint.pin` relative to the PR checkout, so the downgrade lever already existed at the merge gate, and aligning the worker lane is the stated point of #431/#1576. It is also review-visible (a pin edit is a diff hunk). Recorded because the rewritten comment at 2166-2172 asserts the artifact stays 'inside the verification boundary' — true for INTEGRITY, silent about VERSION monotonicity, which is the remaining lever.
issues.fix_hint: Optional hardening, not required for this PR: have registry_selftest_gate compare the tree pin's ACTIONLINT_VERSION against the orchestrator pin's using a component-wise numeric comparator that returns 'unknown' fail-closed (as _python_version_at_least already does) and refuse a strictly LOWER candidate version, or require that a lowered pin also carry the trust-surface label. At minimum, extend the comment at 2166-2172 to state explicitly that version monotonicity is NOT enforced, so the next reader does not infer it from 'the version shape is constrained'. Note scripts/actionlint.pin's own header (line 15) still says the pins are 'NEVER env-supplied' — still literally true (the path is derived from PWD, not the environment), but worth a word now that a caller sets _ACTIONLINT_PIN_FILE.
issues.title: Candidate-controlled actionlint.pin permits a lint DOWNGRADE (bounded, but version-unconstrained)

issues.body:
Line 2470 feeds the candidate's table into _assert_worker_image_gate_deps, but line 1837 still resolves each row through the ORCHESTRATOR revision's _selftest_requirement_apt_package (1818), which hard-codes only command|jq and pymodule|yaml and returns 1 on anything else.

Consequence: a PR that legitimately adds a row to SELFTEST_ENV_REQUIREMENTS, teaches _selftest_requirement_apt_package the new package, AND provisions it in containers/worker-model.Dockerfile is still refused by its own author-side gate, because the mapping consulted is the pre-merge one. The die string then reads 'worker model image final stage does not provision every SELFTEST_ENV_REQUIREMENTS dependency', which names the wrong culprit — the image is fine; the orchestrator's mapping is stale. Same misattribution class #1834 fixed for the behind-base manifest case.

Direction is fail-CLOSED (unknown row -> return 1 -> die), it only fires when the Dockerfile is touched, and the ENV-BLOCKED preflight would refuse such a PR anyway, so this is not blocking.
issues.fix_hint: Either distinguish the two failure modes inside _assert_worker_image_gate_deps — return a distinct status (or print a distinct line) when _selftest_requirement_apt_package refuses a row, and have the gate die naming 'the gate's package mapping does not know requirement <label>; this row cannot be graded until the orchestrator revision learns it' — or parse the mapping's case arms out of the target tree's worker-live.sh the same way _selftest_env_requirements_from_script parses the table.
issues.title: Requirement TABLE moved to the tree but the apt-package MAPPING did not — a PR adding a dependency row cannot pass its own gate, and the refusal misattributes the cause

issues.body:
Lines 4320 and 4331 assert grep counts of 0 against `declare -f` output. A 0-count assertion is vacuous unless the pattern is shown to be capable of matching the RENDERED form of the code it forbids. Lines 4323-4325 do exactly that for the actionlint detector via `legacy_actionlint_body`; the '"$SELFTEST_ENV_REQUIREMENTS" "$SCRIPT_DIR"' detector (4320) and the '_assert_worker_image_gate_deps "$name" ||' detector (4331) have no such fixture.

Both patterns look like they would match bash's declare -f re-rendering (quotes around expansion-bearing words are preserved and continuations are folded onto one line), so I do not believe they are vacuous today — but that is my inference, not an assertion the suite makes. Note also that 4323-4325's fixture greps a hand-written literal rather than declare -f output, so even that one proves the pattern is matchable, not that declare -f renders the legacy code that way.
issues.fix_hint: Add two one-line fixtures alongside `legacy_actionlint_body` — and better, build them by actually defining a throwaway function with the legacy body and grepping `declare -f` of it, which pins the RENDERING rather than just the pattern. E.g. define `_legacy_gate_shape() { ... }` in the self-test carrying the pre-#1576 lines, then assert grep -c over `$(declare -f _legacy_gate_shape)` is 1 for each of the two forbidden patterns.
issues.title: Two negative wiring assertions lack the non-vacuity fixture their sibling has

issues.body: Line 1831 uses `:-`, which treats an explicitly-passed empty string identically to an omitted argument and substitutes the orchestrator-revision table. The only production call site (2470) passes $tree_env_requirements, which _selftest_env_requirements_from_script guarantees is non-empty (it refuses when matches[0].strip() is falsy), so the path is unreachable today. But the whole point of the parameter is 'grade with the CANDIDATE's policy, never the orchestrator's', and `:-` is the one spelling that quietly violates that if a future caller ever passes through an unset or blanked variable.
issues.fix_hint: Use `${2-$SELFTEST_ENV_REQUIREMENTS}` (omitted-only default) so an explicitly empty table reaches the `[[ ${#packages[@]} -gt 0 ]] || return 1` refusal at line 1840 instead of silently reverting to the orchestrator table. The other new call sites already pass the parsed tree value positionally, so no caller changes are needed.
issues.title: `table=${2:-$SELFTEST_ENV_REQUIREMENTS}` silently falls back to the orchestrator table on an EMPTY explicit argument

verdict.summary:
Independently re-verified at head 7bab8b1c2; the diff is unchanged from round 6, so the findings below are the same set at the same severities (hence 'stagnant', not a regression).

The fix is sound and addresses a real fail-open. worker-live.sh:11 sets SCRIPT_DIR from $0 (the ORCHESTRATOR checkout) while the gate runs with PWD at the candidate checkout (git status/bash -n/py_compile in registry_selftest_gate are all PWD-relative), so run_enrolled_selftest's root default (line 1199) meant a candidate's changed self-test was never the suite that actually ran. The diff routes every suite-DESCRIBING input through the tree under test (tree_suite, tree_env_requirements, tree_scripts, tree actionlint.pin) while leaving every CHECK on the trusted orchestrator side (_registry_selftest_targets, _assert_dockerfile_pinned, _assert_workflow_actions_pinned, _selftest_requirement_apt_package). That trusted-check / candidate-data split is the right boundary.

Fail-closed re-verified: the new reader parses and never sources (single re.findall on a column-0 literal; I confirmed exactly one such line exists at 1634-1635 and that the multi-line value round-trips); missing/duplicated/unterminated/empty all return 1 and the gate dies. Nothing candidate-controlled is EXECUTED before the ENV-BLOCKED preflight. _ensure_actionlint's arch guard keys on $# -eq 0, so the env-prefix override preserves it, and the same idiom is already proven at line 5356; the fixed rhysd/actionlint release path and both digests still bound the artifact.

Tests are non-vacuous: accept + three distinct refusal fixtures; the 4298 round-trip against the live table would red on a static-parse-vs-runtime divergence in the CANDIDATE's own script (it runs under the candidate's SCRIPT_DIR); 5434 proves the new table parameter is really used (same Dockerfile flips absent->provisioned).
